new_statements.quote: El patrón de acentuación en todas las variantes del idioma kaqchikel es fijo, su función es demarcativa y su posición es en sílaba final (acento agudo o último). Es invariable en el proceso de derivación. Por eso, no es necesaria su escritura, porque es predecible y no ejerce función distintiva. [...] [p.56] De acuerdo al informe de la Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel, además de registrar el acento fijo (agudo o último) también se registra los patrones de acentuación: acento penúltimo y acento en sílaba pesada, que ocurren en muy pocas palabras y en algunas variantes. [...] a) El acento penúltimo, que no es muy común en la mayoría de variantes, ocurre en algunas palabras propias del Kaqchikel y en algunas palabras prestadas del castellano que son palabras graves.
new_statements.translation: The stress pattern in all variants of the Kaqchikel language is fixed; its function is demarcative and its position is on the final syllable (acute/last-syllable stress). It is invariant under derivation. Therefore it need not be written, because it is predictable and has no distinctive function. [...] According to the report of the Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel, besides fixed (final) stress, two further patterns are recorded: penultimate stress and stress on a heavy syllable, which occur in very few words and in some variants. [...] a) Penultimate stress, which is not very common in most variants, occurs in some native Kaqchikel words and in some Spanish loanwords that are paroxytone.
new_statements.citation: Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel (Academia de Lenguas Mayas de Guatemala); J. E. Ajsivinac Sián, Lolmay P. O. García Mátzar, M. Chacach Cutzal, I. E. Alonzo Guaján. 2004. Gramática descriptiva del idioma maya Kaqchikel: Rutzijoxik rucholik ri Kaqchikel ch'ab'äl. Chimaltenango: CLK-ALMG.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Copies checked ( present, large files hardlinked with kaqc1278/kaqc1275; the target record's 'held' list is empty only because the our source list snapshot predates the save). (1) Quote: I read the page renders printed p.55) and p.56) of the CLK-ALMG 2004 'Gramatica descriptiva del idioma maya Kaqchikel'. Under the heading 'Acento' p.55 reads exactly: 'El patron de acentuacion en todas las variantes del idioma kaqchikel es fijo, su funcion es demarcativa y su posicion es en silaba final (acento agudo o ultimo). Es invariable en el proceso de derivacion. Por eso, no es necesaria su escritura, porque es predecible y no ejerce funcion distintiva.' followed by underlined final syllables (nupatz…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the final syllable of the word (roots, derived words and compounds alike; derivational suffixes take the stress), in every Kaqchikel variety including Acatenango; it is predictable and non-contrastive.
new_statements.secondary_stress: ALMG 2004 says nothing about secondary stress. Bennett 2018 (Glossa 3(1):67, fn.7) states secondary stress has never been reported for Kaqchikel and finds no phonotactic evidence for it; multi-word compounds may carry one final stress per prosodic word.
new_statements.exceptions: Penultimate stress in a handful of native words (vakix 'cow', tukur 'owl', tata 'señor', nana 'señora', b'alam 'jaguar', anxa 'garlic', janila 'much') and in Spanish loans (anma, paxa, alb'ertix, xalma); 'acento en sílaba pesada' in very few transitive verb forms in the variants of Santa María de Jesús, Antigua Guatemala, Parramos, San Bartolomé and Magdalena Milpas Altas (not Acatenango). OKMA 1997:20 adds that enclitics on verbs/statives attract the stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement (palabra: radical, derivada o compuesta), illustrated with citation forms; Bennett 2018 identifies the domain as the prosodic word. Brown et al. 2006 (via Nelson 2020) add that phrasal primary stress falls on the last word.
new_statements.identity_note: kaqc1277 'Kaqchikel, Akatenango Southwestern' is a retired Ethnologue/ISO dialect code [ckk] (Ethnologue 15: municipio and town of Acatenango, Chimaltenango; pop. 500), merged into Kaqchikel [cak] = Glottolog kaqc1270 in 2009. No Acatenango-specific phonological description exists (Glottolog 0 refs; Ethnologue 15 lists no bibliography; only Kaufman's 1970 PLFM handwritten survey questionnaire documents the variety). The quoted statement is a Kaqchikel-language-level rule from the ALMG 2004 descriptive grammar, which explicitly asserts it for 'todas las variantes' and whose dialect data include Acatenango; the heavy-syllable exception it lists is confined to Sacatepéquez towns, not Acatenango. A catalog entry should be filed at language level (kaqc1270) or flagged as inherited from it.

sources.note: sec.3.1: 'Stress in Kaqchikel is quite uniform, falling mostly on word-final syllables, with only a very small handful of exceptions showing non-final stress'; tense/lax vowel contrast only in stressed (final) syllables.

sources.citation: Bennett, Ryan. 2018. Recursive prosodic words in Kaqchikel (Mayan). Glossa: a journal of general linguistics 3(1): 67, 1-33. doi:10.5334/gjgl.550

sources.note: pp.11-12: domain of stress is the prosodic word; 'stress is basically restricted to word-final position in Kaqchikel'; fn.7: secondary stress has never been reported for Kaqchikel, lax vowels and [ʔC] clusters (stress diagnostics) occur only in stressed word-final syllables, 'safest to assume that there is no word-level secondary stress'; compounds may contain multiple prosodic words each with its own (final) stress.

sources.note: p.55: stress in ALL Kaqchikel variants is fixed, demarcative, on the final syllable ('acento agudo o último'), invariant under derivation, predictable and non-distinctive so not. p.56: penultimate stress in a few native words (vakix, tukur, tata, nana, b'alam, anxa, janila) and Spanish loans; 'acento en sílaba pesada' in very few words in Santa María de Jesús, Antigua, Parramos, S. Bartolomé and Magdalena Milpas Altas. The grammar's dialect data (Informe de Variación Dialectal de la CLK) explicitly include Acatenango.

sources.note: p.20: 'El Kaqchikel se caracteriza por tener acento fijo.. El acento es agudo, lo que significa que la acentuación siempre va a recaer en la sílaba final de la palabra (radical, derivada o compuesta..)'; enclitics added to verbs and statives attract the stress; no orthographic tilde needed because position is predictable (final syllable).
